\begin{tablenotes}\footnotesize
\item Local users are split into random halves A and B (3 splits, averaged); half A is the reference of every comparison. Two-sided matched: half B and the foreign data are both reduced to $V=\min(n_B, n_F)$ shared-product interactions by adding whole users in random order and stopping before the user who would exceed $V$ (10 draws per split). Null foreign: the foreign user$\times$product matrix randomised by curveball trades ($5\times$ users per draw, 10 draws), preserving every product's and user's interaction count; the matched null uses the same users as the matched foreign sample. In matched rows, Local is half B after downsampling (equal to half B when half B is the smaller side). Ratio = $F/L$ over pairs with local agreement $L$ at or above the threshold (pairs in parentheses). $D=F-L$ uses all pairs; $D>0$ = share of pairs where foreign agreement exceeds local agreement. Chance level $c$: the null agreement for pattern measures; 0 for rank correlation and $10/n$ for top-10 overlap ($n$ = shared products), because the null leaves popularity agreement unchanged. Chance-corrected values use pairs with $L-c\ge0.05$. Medians over pairs; 95\% CIs from the two-way cluster bootstrap (countries, with target and donor sharing a draw, and categories).
\end{tablenotes}
\end{table}
